# int/float kind, precision, and the loud refusals.
# expected forms: canonical decode render (README §data.tsv), or
# `ERR <code>` (the number converter refuses a claimed spelling), or bare
# `ERR` (jsonic itself rejects; its message is dependency-native and

column3: a dot keeps Float (the collapse StructUtil.parse regressed on once)
trailing-dot exponent is ONE Float token
exponent without a dot stays Integer

column1: # § loud numeric refusals — the converter, not the jsonic parse

column3: data decode refuses a receiverless leading dot
binary64 overflow stays loud, never Inf
signed leading-dot spelling is refused whole
…and a nested refusal surfaces from inside a list

column1: # § the lenient jsonic superset — digit-led prose stays ONE string

column3: never an error, never a split
a top-level run never splits into a stray list
empty exponent after a dot declines to text
signed leading-dot run with following text declines whole
language operators are plain text in a data grammar

column1: # § structure, order, and the non-numeric scalars

column3: Float and Integer side by side
data context: quoted text stays a string, never a word
top-level null decodes to the concrete none
jsonic's lenient trailing comma is part of the superset
malformed structure is refused by jsonic itself

column1: # § base-prefixed prose — a run that is not a COMPLETE base-prefixed token
# declines to the stock scanners, which agree on it in both ports. (They
# did not until jsonic v0.6.0 / parser v0.8.0: the TS scanner split such a
# run into stray values, and a boru matcher arm claimed the whole run to
# hide it. Fixed upstream, arm retired — ADR-014. These rows are the pin.)

column3: a dot-adjacent hex run stays ONE lenient string in both ports
…and never sheds stray values into a list
octal with a dotted exponent tail
separator inside the claimed prose run
an EMPTY body declines to stock text (the scanners agree there)

column1: # § insertion-ordered maps — integer-like keys included. A plain JS object
# enumerates these ascending whatever the source wrote, so the TS seam
# records the true order for its runner to read (Go reads OrderedMap.Keys).

column3: source order survives, not numeric order
…with a wider integer key ahead of a narrower one
…and a string key ahead of an integer-like one

column1: # § sign+separator runs — a separator is legal only BETWEEN digits, so these
# are lenient text in both ports rather than numbers (the stock Go scanner
# used to read `+_1` as 1, silently swallowing the `+_`).

column3: a separator after the sign is text, never the number 1
but a DIGIT-led run is still claimed and refused loudly

column1: # § lowercase-only prefixes, at the data seam too — loud, not a lenient
#   string, which is the one place the jsonic superset gives way.

column3: uppercase hex is refused in a data decode as well
